instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Start the Hard Part
cards.instruction: Get someone else to explain, announce, or begin the emotionally difficult part.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You tell the choir the tour's cancelled. Say 'cancelled', not 'on hold'; I'll handle the refund forms.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're the organiser. They should hear it from you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which is why I must get these amounts right. Start with the cancellation, pause, then mention refunds. Please don't improvise a cheerful opening.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They'll ask whether we'll ever tour again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say we can't promise that. Let them finish reacting before you call me over. I'll be ready with the exact amount each person gets back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Phone Mum about selling the house. Start with the upkeep, please, not property prices. You have to prepare her properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She asked to speak to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And she will. First say the repairs are too much, then the word 'selling'. Don't offer a date; I'll handle the details.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm putting her on speaker. I'm not taking all the shouting while you hide.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. Keep it on speaker. But don't say 'we've something to tell you'; say 'selling the house'. I'll come in once she's answered that.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: What Aren’t You Saying?
cards.instruction: Find out what someone is holding back by treating every careful answer as incomplete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: 'Interesting' isn't audition feedback. Give me one thing to keep and one to change, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're my sister. I'm trying to encourage you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then make the encouragement usable. Start with the singing, then the dancing. Please don't skip the part that made you wince.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your singing was better than your dancing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Better is a comparison, not a diagnosis. Was I late on the turns or unable to do them? I need to know what you're protecting me from.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: These minutes say 'a proposal was discussed'. Mine. Minutes need names and decisions, please. What happened to both?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sign them and we can eat. Nobody wanted an awkward record.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: 'Nobody' isn't a list of attendees. Who asked you to remove my name? Please answer that before reaching for the pen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I did. I suggested someone else present it so the proposal had a chance.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Name the presenter, please. And what is the objection to me presenting it? 'Had a chance' is another outcome without a reason.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Hope with Me
cards.instruction: Recruit someone into believing that the outcome can still change, even when the evidence is thin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two streets rejected our parade route, not the whole town. Please rub out 'cancelled' and help me find a third.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The only route left goes behind the supermarket.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then draw it properly, including the loading bay. Not a dotted line. It's a possible route until someone tells us otherwise. Who might watch there?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My dad would. He works in the warehouse.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put him by the staff entrance, clear of the parade. Good. Now put someone beside him; he won't be the only worker coming out for a look.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Help me choose glasses for our cafe. Hold them by the base, please; we need to see how they'll look on the tables.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're only on the waiting list. I haven't even told Mum.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Waiting isn't rejected. Please assess the glass, not the application. Picture someone sitting at our table: what would you serve them in?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum would want a mug. She hates tea in glass.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then find her a mug. Not that tiny one; she'll want to stay. Put it beside our two glasses so we can see the whole table.

cards.title: Say the Scary Part
cards.instruction: Get someone else to name the frightening possibility or vulnerable feeling before you do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we open the landlord's letter, state the worst possible outcome for our shop. Out loud, please. We should assess this properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've only missed one payment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the current position, not an outcome. Please finish the sentence: 'If we can't pay, we could...'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Lose the shop. Dad would understand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't skip to reassuring me. What would I have done to the business he trusted me with? Say that first; then we'll open it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we go on for the skating qualifier, name the outcome we haven't prepared for. We need a complete plan, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't want to put failure in your head.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's already there. Saying 'failure' isn't specific enough. Finish this: 'We might not...'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Qualify. I'd still want to skate with you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Keep that promise. Now say what you think I'm afraid you'd do if we didn't qualify.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: See What This Took
cards.instruction: Make someone recognize the courage, restraint, or emotional labor your choices required.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Here's the apology I sent you. This closed envelope holds the draft I didn't send. Compare the thickness, please, not the wording.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I appreciate the apology. Why show me the envelope?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because you're evaluating the result without the work. One paragraph sent; six pages withheld. Please count the restraint as well as the words.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now I want to know what was on those six pages.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then put the envelope down, please. Those are the words I worked all night not to give you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I told the committee I won't chair another year. Two sentences, no apology. Please notice what I managed to leave out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Good. Could you stay until we find someone?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's not what the sentences say. Read them again. I practised in your car for an hour to stop adding 'unless you need me'.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll tell them you're exhausted and need a break.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No explanation, please. You're putting back the part I worked to remove. Tell them I said no, and tell me you heard how hard that was.
